name: forward_argument_to_library_stub
description: Passes its one incoming argument, a library base pointer read from a global variable, and the address of its own stack argument to the library call stub at offset minus 132.

name: measure_stack_string_and_forward
description: Calls a function pointer stored in a global variable, then counts the characters of a 140-byte stack buffer up to its null terminator. If the count is nonzero it passes the buffer and the count to another routine.

name: store_byte_through_a3_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of data register D0 to the memory address held in address register A3 and returns. Its only caller is the library call stub at offset minus 132.

name: parse_command_line_and_start
description: Program entry that opens the dos library and allocates a control block, then splits the command line into argument strings, honoring double quotes and asterisk escapes. It then runs the main routine and releases the file and buffer resources it opened.

name: release_file_and_library_state
description: Fetches a state pointer from a global library base, stores the given value in it, and conditionally closes a file, closes a library, frees memory and replies to a message based on flags in that state. It returns the value it was given.

name: run_file_pager_session
description: Sets up a pager session for one file, allocating its control block, opening the file and an output window, and choosing the display mode from the arguments. It then loops showing pages until quit, with prompts for the file name, percentage shown, end of file and binary content warnings.

name: reschedule_four_global_slots
description: Calls the reschedule library stub four times, each time pairing a field of its structure argument with one of four consecutive global words.

name: scan_buffer_for_control_bytes
description: Fills a buffer of 80 bytes through another routine, makes a second call with zero and minus-one arguments, then scans the bytes. It returns 1 at the first byte in the ranges 1 to 7, 14 to 26, 28 to 31 or 128 to 159, and 0 if none appear.

name: dispatch_pager_key_input
description: Waits for a console input signal, reads one key and dispatches it through a large switch on character codes. The cases cover escape sequences, a slash that reads a search pattern, the letter h and other commands.

name: call_through_address_register
description: Calls a routine with a global argument, calls a second routine, then jumps through a function pointer held in address register A3. The strings in this file mention editor and previous-page prompts, but the decompiled body shows only these calls, so the purpose is not confirmed.

name: initialize_session_and_loop
description: Sets a counter to 1 and clears a flag in its structure, stores a routine result in one field, and repeats another routine call while the counter stays positive and a size comparison holds.

name: update_entity_and_increment_counter
description: Calls two routines on a buffer inside its structure and stores the second result in a field of that structure. When a flag field is zero it also increments a short counter reached through a pointer stored in the structure.

name: read_line_convert_formfeed
description: Reads up to 128 bytes into a buffer, scans to the next newline or form-feed, and repositions the stream past that line. A form-feed is replaced by the two characters caret and L followed by a newline, and a flag is set.

name: run_step_loop_until_quit
description: Runs a loop of 9, 13 or 14 steps, with the count chosen by flags in its structure, calling routines from a global table of pointers on each step. It stops and calls a cleanup routine with zero when the key is the letter q or control-C, code 3.

name: search_stream_until_match
description: Formats a search message from a flag-selected global string, then reads and tests the stream until a match is found or the attempt counter drops below one. It returns 1 on a match and 0 on failure.

name: wrap_call_with_setup_teardown
description: Runs a setup call, a call using its structure and a global, and an optional second global call. It then makes the main call with its second argument, runs a teardown call with minus one, and returns the main call's result.

name: call_pair_then_flagged_once
description: Calls another routine with two arguments, then calls it again with its first argument alone only when a short flag at offset 98 in the structure is zero.

name: call_stream_then_window_bound
description: Calls one routine with a stream handle field, a second field and minus one, then calls another routine with a window bound value read through a structure pointer.

name: call_stream_then_decrement_bound
description: Calls one routine with a stream handle field, zero and one, then calls another routine with the window's bound value minus one.

name: display_text_lines_up_to_count
description: Reads text in chunks of at most 128 bytes and counts newline characters until the requested number of lines is reached. A form-feed sets a flag that stops the output, and the routine calls stream routines at each step.

name: reschedule_with_structure_field
description: Passes its second argument to another routine, then calls the reschedule stub with the structure's field at offset 16, a global address and its first argument.

name: mark_flag_then_forward
description: Sets a short value in a linked structure to one when a field at offset 4 is zero, then calls the reschedule stub with the structure's field at offset 16 and a global address.

name: select_reschedule_arguments_by_flag
description: Chooses its second and third arguments by a flag in its structure: either two global addresses, or a global address and a window bound plus one. It calls the reschedule stub with these and the structure's field at offset 16.

name: reschedule_with_flag_arguments
description: Calls the reschedule stub with a structure field and either three global addresses or one global address and a window bound value, chosen by a flag in the structure.

name: call_twice_and_clamp_result
description: Calls another routine twice with the same first argument and different trailing arguments, then returns the second result with any negative value replaced by zero.

name: consume_buffered_bytes
description: Copies up to the requested number of bytes from the structure's buffer into the destination, refilling through another routine first when the buffer is short. It advances the read offset and position fields, reduces the remaining count and returns the number of bytes consumed.

name: refill_read_buffer
description: When the 4096-byte read buffer is exactly full, passes its pending bytes to another routine first. It then reads more data into the free space, resets the offset and position fields, and returns the number of bytes read.

name: update_scroll_window
description: Computes a target scroll position from its offset argument, then compares it with the visible window range in its structure. When the target is outside that range it resets or moves the window fields and calls another routine, and it returns minus one for an invalid mode.

name: read_line_into_buffer
description: Reads characters one at a time through another routine into a destination buffer, storing the newline and stopping there or after 127 characters. It appends a null terminator and returns the number of characters stored.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source string to a destination one at a time, including the terminating null byte.

name: convert_string_to_uppercase
description: Converts each lowercase ASCII letter in a null-terminated string to uppercase in place by subtracting 32, and leaves all other characters unchanged.

name: parse_signed_decimal_string
description: Reads an optional plus or minus sign followed by decimal digits from a string and returns the signed integer value. Parsing stops at the first character that is not a digit.

name: call_library_if_pointers_set
description: Calls a library routine with a pointer from its structure, its first argument and minus one, but only when that first argument and the structure's field at offset 4 are both nonzero.

name: close_pager_state_and_free
description: Tears down a pager session by closing its file and window handles and restoring saved pointers, with a nonempty text argument and a flag causing input to be read until a newline. It then releases the structure's 4924-byte memory block.

name: call_with_single_value_buffer

name: allocate_block_and_copy_fields
description: Allocates a 36-byte block and, if that succeeds, passes a value derived from its address to a library call through a stack buffer. It copies two fields from the block into the caller's structure, frees the block, and returns the library call's result.

name: create_block_from_source_words
description: Allocates a 68-byte object, copies a given number of words from a source array into it, and links it to a handle from another routine. It passes the object on, releases the handle, then frees the object and returns a field read from it earlier.

description: Calls a library routine at offset minus 96 from a library base pointer held in a global variable. It passes no arguments and returns nothing.

name: divide_32_bit_unsigned
description: Divides a 32-bit unsigned value in D1 by the divisor in D2 and returns the quotient and remainder in two registers. For divisors above 65535 it uses bit-by-bit shift and subtract steps, and for smaller divisors it uses 16-bit divide operations.

name: multiply_32_bit_integers
description: Multiplies the 32-bit values in D0 and D1 from their 16-bit halves and returns the low 32 bits of the product. It also returns D1 with its two 16-bit halves swapped.

name: negate_result_on_flag
description: Calls another routine and returns its first result, negated when the second result register is nonzero.

name: validate_disk_allocation_bitmap
description: Program entry for Disk-Validator that walks ranges of disk blocks, compares each block's bit in a bitmap against the expected allocation bitmap, and records mismatches. It also writes status digits into an output buffer, and an unrecovered jump table leaves some dispatch unclear.

name: call_copymem_then_indirect_jump
description: Calls the Exec CopyMem function through an exec base pointer kept in a global variable, at offset minus 624, then makes an indirect call to an unrecovered target. The purpose of that second call cannot be determined from this code.

name: reset_blit_state_at_entry
description: Program entry for AM2_BLIT that calls routines and a library function in a loop from 9 down to 6, then clears a word at a fixed location. If a stored memory word matches a constant it swaps that word with a global variable and clears the global; the library facts list exec.FreeMem.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter register in a loop until it reaches minus one, then returns. It is a plain countdown with no other effect.

name: unpack_stream_and_clear_cache
description: Runs seven passes of bit-driven copying within a buffer, which looks like a decompression loop, then calls the Exec CacheClearU function when a 16-bit global field exceeds 36.

name: decode_bitstream_length_code
description: Decodes a variable-length code from a packed bit stream using a small table of global bytes, and stores the result in a global counter. It then copies that many bytes backward within the buffer as part of the unpacking.

name: expand_packed_bitstream_block
description: Repeatedly reads length and distance codes from a packed bit stream and copies earlier output bytes within the buffer, updating a global count. It is the main loop of the unpacking scheme used by the cache-clearing routine.

name: decode_distance_code_from_bits
description: Decodes a distance value from a packed bit stream using a small table of global bytes to choose a bit count and base, and returns it in a register. The unpacking routines call it to get each back-reference distance.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only a bad-instruction marker remains in this entry, so it is bad data rather than working code. It has no behaviour to describe.

name: clear_cpu_state_at_entry
description: Program entry for AM2_CPU that calls routines and a library function in a loop from 8 down to 5, then clears a word at a fixed location. If a stored memory word matches a constant it swaps that word with a global variable and clears the global; the library facts list exec.FreeMem.

name: decrement_until_minus_one

name: reset_game_state_at_entry

name: decrement_until_minus_one

name: parse_command_line_and_start
description: Program entry for the Avail utility that opens the dos library and allocates a control block, then splits the command line into argument strings, honoring double quotes and asterisk escapes. It then runs the main routine and releases the resources it opened.

name: release_file_and_library_state
description: Fetches a state pointer from a global library base, stores the given value in it, and conditionally closes a file, closes a library, frees memory and replies to a message based on flags in that state. It returns the value it was given.

name: sum_memory_region_sizes_by_flag
description: Walks a linked list of memory region records and adds up the size of each region whose flag bits overlap the given mask. It returns the total.

name: print_memory_availability_table
description: Prints a memory table with Type, Available, In-Use, Maximum and Largest columns for chip, fast and total memory. The figures come from library queries for each memory type, and the argument can restrict the output to one type.

name: forward_with_stack_slot_pointer
description: Passes its two arguments to another routine together with a pointer to a fixed slot 12 bytes into the caller's stack frame. It returns nothing.

name: measure_stack_string_and_forward
description: Calls a function pointer from a global variable to fill a 140-byte stack buffer, then counts the characters up to the null terminator. If the count is nonzero it passes the buffer and the count to another routine.

name: add_disk_buffers_to_device
description: Program entry for the addbuffers command: it reads the DRIVE and BUFFERS arguments, checks the named device, and reports either its current buffer count or an invalid device or volume error. It then adds the requested buffers through dos library calls.
